solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

flags: minor: three distractors (strident, cursory, dogmatic) are all negative and clearly contradicted by 'weighs several explanations'; only 'measured' fits the positive, cautious context, making it a fairly one-step item
S003-01.notes: Weighing several explanations and admitting limits of the evidence = measured/restrained; contrasts with single-cause earlier accounts. Dogmatic is the opposite; cursory contradicts careful weighing; strident is tone mismatch.

S003-02.notes: Text 2 grants that travel times improve at first (so the one-year data are accurate) but says congestion returns within a few years; the planners' one-year window is too short. A contradicts 'improve at first'; B contradicts more people driving; C unsupported.

flags: minor: B and D are mirror images (same frame, towns swapped), which signals that one of the pair is the key
S003-03.notes: Increases: A +3,000 (25%), B +4,500 (15%), C +2,400 (30%). Largest percent = C, largest number = B. D swaps them; C compares the wrong towns and doesn't address percent; A ignores change.

S003-04.notes: Inverted sentence: subject is 'a set of bronze navigational dividers' (singular head 'set'), so singular past 'was'. Trap: 'hundreds of objects' sits before the verb and pulls toward plural 'were'. 'are'/'have been' are plural and tense-inconsistent. Two traps (inversion + 'set of') put it near the medium/hard boundary.

S003-05.notes: Two independent clauses joined by conjunctive adverb 'however', which belongs to the second clause (contrast with expectation): 'repair; however, the anchorages...'. A is a comma splice; B attaches however to the wrong clause; C lacks a proper boundary.

S003-06.notes: Introductory modifier 'Trained as a botanist...' must modify a person, so the subject must be Ines Varga. A and B make the paintings the trained botanist (dangling/misplaced modifier; possessive in A is a common trap); D is ungrammatical/awkward with expletive 'there'.

S003-07.notes: Less steel would suggest lower cost, but it will cost more: concession/contrast -> 'Even so'. Consequently implies cause; In other words implies restatement; Likewise implies similarity.

flags: minor: A is the only choice that mentions both departure and arrival, so it is identifiable by simple goal-matching
S003-08.notes: Goal requires contrasting earlier departure with later arrival; only A has both pieces linked by 'Although'. C omits departure; D omits arrival; B is irrelevant.

S003-09.notes: Without crabs, snails graze open plots bare; with abundant snail-eating crabs, open plots look like fenced ones, implying predators keep snail grazing in check. B invents crab grazing; C is backwards (fences make little difference where crabs abound); D overstates ('entirely', 'anywhere').

flags: minor: the hypothesis has two parts (learning from adults + founder effect); C targets the learning part, which is adequate, but a careful reader might note C does not say the lab birds match rural pitch, only that they are lower than city birds
S003-10.notes: If pitch is learned from adults, chicks raised by city adults should sing at city pitch even in quiet. C shows they sing lower without noise, implicating noise rather than learning. A is consistent with learning; B (adults don't change) is consistent with Mensah and if anything weakens the noise view; D bears on noise, not on Mensah's hypothesis directly.

S003-11.notes: 'However' after the critics' claim of declining ambition; heavy revision of sparse passages suggests effort/ambition, challenging the critics. A: sketchbooks don't explain why; B is the opposite; C wrong technique claim.
